definitions.explanation: Describes someone who lacks skill or ability in something. The opposite of {上手|じょうず} (skillful). Can be self-deprecating when used about oneself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下手|へた}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦すみません→すみません：00998_sumimasen⟧。
{下手|へた}で⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{挑戦|ちょうせん}→挑戦：03495_chousen⟧⟦しよう→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Even if I'm not good at it, let's give it a try.

notes:
{下手|へた} is a na-adjective meaning unskillful or bad at something.

COMMON PATTERNS:
〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下手|へた}です: to be bad at ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧: skillful, good at (opposite)
- ⟦{得意|とくい}→得意：03455_tokui⟧: strong point, good at (confidence-based)
- ⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧: not good at, weak point (broader than skill — includes dislike)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese modesty (⟦{謙遜|けんそん}→謙遜：04142_kenson⟧) means people commonly say {下手|へた}です about their own abilities, even when skilled. This is polite, not necessarily literal.

WATCH OUT:
Avoid using {下手|へた} directly about others — it can sound blunt or rude. ⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧ or ⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧ are softer alternatives.

FORMS:
- {下手|へた}な〜: unskillful ~ (modifier)
- {下手|へた}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: clumsily, poorly (adverbial)

cross_references.label: weak point, not good at, unskillful
